cover.headline: 14 stories in 5 minutes. Fears of a strike on Iran, mass protests in Europe, Brazil and Serbia vote.

stories.head: Trump muses about "another little Epic Fury"
body: US envoy Tom Barrack says a strike this weekend is possible, though Trump has said any attack would wait until after Nov. 3. Iran vows a response several times greater.
Brent settled at $116.72 on Friday. Yemen's Houthis hit Aden airport for the fourth time this month.

stories.head: Mass protests over living costs
body: France: organisers say 800,000 marched, authorities say 410,000. Nearly 1,000 were arrested and 70,000 officers deployed.
Italy: clashes in Rome, Milan and Turin, 371 briefly detained. Tear gas also in Tirana; pensioners marched in Madrid.

stories.head: Jordan church attack, Israel votes Tuesday
body: Three gunmen killed eight at a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church in Karak. No group has claimed it.
Israel: neither bloc is set to reach 61 seats. The West Bank is under closure after two soldiers died near Hebron.

stories.head: Brazil and Serbia go to the polls
body: Brazil: Lula vs. Flavio Bolsonaro, polls close 5 p.m. Brasilia time. Polls missed the first round.
Serbia: Vucic faces a student list. The only October poll had the students 44.5% to 42.7%.

stories.head: Ebola trial, Kim in China, Sudan drought
body: WHO starts the first Ebola vaccine trial of this outbreak in DR Congo. Kenya reports a second death.
Kim Jong Un makes a one-day trip to Dandong. Sudan faces famine risk as rain hits a decades-long low. Seven missing after a Nairobi collapse.
